the Ca2+ switch of zebrafish Rec1a is more sensitive than that of Rec2a, and that the switch of Rec1a resembles more closely the switch of mammalian recoverin than the switches of Rec2a and Rec1b.
the zebrafish ortholog of mammalian recoverin is expressed in different variants that differ with respect to their calcium sensing properties and their calcium switch.
zebrafish Recoverins display differences in Ca2+-switch mechanisms, and that these differences depend on the myristolation of the protein.

a detailed understanding of Ca2+-myr-switch mechanisms of recoverin isoform variants and their functional consequences.

the functional properties of the different zebrafish recovery isoforms and the impact of a myristoyl modification on Ca2+ sensing.

Ca2+ sensing of zRec isoforms is similar to that of bovine recoverin.
zRec1a, 1b, 2a, and 2b differ from bovine recoverin in the way that they sense Ca2+.

zebrafish Rec isoforms are functionally distinct and may serve as a model system for studying the Ca2+-myristol switch mechanism in vivo.
zebrafish isoforms of recoverin are different in terms of Ca2+-switch mechanisms and Ca2+-sensitivity.
recoverin isoforms in zebrafish display a differential response to Ca2+ and that this response is modified by the presence of a myristoyl tail.

recoverin isoforms in zebrafish differ in their Ca2+-sensitivity.
